name: OH HELL
description: Oh Hell (also known as Oh Hell!) is a classic trick-taking card game that emphasizes precision bidding over raw power. Unlike most trick-takers where you try to win as many tricks as possible, the goal is to win exactly the number of tricks you bid. It is famous for its 'River' structure, where hand sizes increase and decrease throughout the game, and its 'Hook' rule that prevents every player from being successful simultaneously.

content.text: Oh Hell (also known as Oh Hell!) is a classic trick-taking card game that emphasizes precision bidding over raw power. Unlike most trick-takers where you try to win as many tricks as possible, the goal is to win exactly the number of tricks you bid. It is famous for its 'River' structure, where hand sizes increase and decrease throughout the game, and its 'Hook' rule that prevents every player from being successful simultaneously.
Believed to have originated in the early 20th century (likely New York clubs), it is a member of the 'Bid Whist' and 'Skat' family but simplified for social play.
From 3 to 7 people can play. The game is best when played with 4 to 6.
52 cards. Rank: A > K > Q > J > 10... > 2.

Varies by round. Round 1: 1 card each. Round 2: 2 cards each. (Ascending up to 10 or 12, then descending back to 1).

items.text: Sequence of hands: Some play 1 up to max then down to 1; some start at max and go down then up (e.g. 7-1-7 or 10-1-10). Maximum cards per hand may be 7, 10, 12, or 13 depending on player count and variant.

Determining trumps: When all cards are dealt there is no card to turn; hand is played at no trump. Some use a fixed rotation of trump suits (e.g. spades, diamonds, clubs, hearts) or include no-trump in the sequence.
Hook and bidding style: Some play without the Hook (dealer may bid so total equals tricks). Some use simultaneous bidding (fists on table, reveal on count) instead of turn-based.
